back: Spermatogonia, spermatocytes, spermatids, spermatozoa, Sertoli cells; interstitial cells lie between tubules.
Spermatogonium (2n, mitosis) → primary spermatocyte (2n) → meiosis I → 2 secondary spermatocytes (n) → meiosis II → 4 spermatids → 4 sperm.
Oogonia (before birth) → primary oocyte (arrested prophase I) → meiosis I → secondary oocyte + polar body → ovulation → meiosis II at fertilisation.
Nourish and protect developing sperm; respond to FSH; secrete inhibin.
Secrete testosterone in response to LH.
The ovum keeps most cytoplasm, food and organelles for the early embryo; polar bodies degenerate.

front: Which cell is released at ovulation?
back: A secondary oocyte arrested at metaphase II.
GnRH → FSH and LH; LH → testosterone; FSH + testosterone → spermatogenesis; testosterone and inhibin feed back negatively.
